book.title: The Girl Who Sat Alone at Lunch
book.author: Jun Hartley

lines: Day one at the new school, I ate my sandwich in the library bathroom stall, like a spy who had lost the plot.
Day two, I tried the bench by the football field and was nearly knocked out by a ball and a boy shouting "sorry!" in a voice that sounded suspiciously like "serves you right."
On day three I found the empty music room on the third floor, and a piano with a sticky E.
I played for the whole lunch with the sandwich propped on top.
The next day I heard someone breathing at the door.
A girl with a clarinet case and enormous earrings.
"You're doing the second bar wrong," she said.
Nobody tells you that being alone is only a waiting room.
That the day comes when someone opens the door and says you're doing the second bar wrong, and it's the nicest thing anyone has said to you all term.
